paragraphs: Seder HaDorot, under the entry “Savar” [סבר], cites a story about him. He was a great sage, but Hyman says he has kept this notice brief because he did not find him in the midrashim.[^1][^2]

notes.text: בסה״ד is contextually Seder HaDorot, not the superseded Sefer HaDorot guess, without fresh edition identification. ערך סבר remains entry Savar with literal Hebrew; its vowels and entry relation are unverified.

מעשה ממנו can be a story about/from him; the body’s about is the contextual reading, not a source collation. Supplied חכם differs from machine חנם. Hyman’s own first-person קצרתי and absence from midrashim are attributed to him, not a new exhaustive search. Great sage supplies no separate Rabbi title; Layish is conventional vocalization only.
